guide.title: Haydn: String Quartet Op. 76 No. 3 – IV. Finale (Presto)
guide.overview: This fast finale starts in the dark key of C minor. It ends in bright C major. Listen for the opening tune, which comes back in the middle of the second part. Listen also for the shift to a new section near the end. Keys and chords here are estimated by computer, so small details may be off.

listening_points.headline: The opening tune in C minor
listening_points.text: The first violin plays the main tune [m. 1-4]. All the instruments move together in block chords. This is called homophonic texture. It starts loud, then drops to soft [m. 2].

listening_points.headline: Loud and soft contrasts, with a brief visit to F minor
listening_points.text: The first violin mostly sings over an accompaniment, and the cello briefly takes the tune [m. 13]. The music flips between loud and soft. It touches F minor for a moment [m. 8-9]. It returns to C minor and turns loud at [m. 12].

listening_points.headline: Key changes brighten and darken the mood
listening_points.text: The music turns to G major, where the viola probably leads [m. 18-19]. Then it moves through G minor, E-flat major and F minor. The sound stays loud. A sharp accent marked fz lands in F minor [m. 26].

listening_points.headline: A quiet, lighter patch in B-flat major
listening_points.text: The volume drops to soft [m. 28]. The key is B-flat major, which sounds gentler. The first violin probably keeps the tune. Instruments weave separate lines in the later bars [m. 33-36].

listening_points.headline: Settling in E-flat major, then turning loud
listening_points.text: The music rests in E-flat major for a long stretch. It is soft at first. It turns loud at [m. 46], with the first violin clearly in front. The computer estimates the busiest point of Part 1 at [m. 56]. It is marked f, like the bars around it.

listening_points.headline: Tune passed around, then soft and loud endings to Part 1
listening_points.text: The second violin and first violin trade the lead in short bits [m. 58-61]. The cello takes over briefly [m. 62-63]. The music gets soft at [m. 68] and stays soft through [m. 71a]. The bar labelled [m. 72b] is loud. Part 1 is repeated.

listening_points.headline: Part 2 begins loud and moves through new keys
listening_points.text: Part 2 starts loud [m. 73]. It reaches a soft B-flat major passage [m. 79]. Then it jumps to loud again with a return to E-flat major [m. 83-84]. From [m. 84] the second violin probably leads, but the lead is unclear.

listening_points.headline: Wandering through A-flat major and back
listening_points.text: The music moves to A-flat major [m. 87]. It briefly dips into C minor [m. 92]. It returns to E-flat and A-flat [m. 94-97]. Lead passes quickly between the two violins [m. 98-103]. Accents (fz) mark B-flat major [m. 107-109].

listening_points.headline: Back to C minor, still loud
listening_points.text: The key returns to C minor [m. 110]. It stays loud, with the first violin mostly in front, right up to the return of the opening tune.

listening_points.headline: The opening tune returns
listening_points.text: Here is the moment to catch. The first violin plays the main tune again, in C minor, exactly as at the start [m. 119-122]. It drops to soft at [m. 120].

listening_points.headline: The opening pattern again, then the quietest point
listening_points.text: The music follows the earlier pattern, then moves to F minor [m. 126]. Single lines appear alone [m. 130, 133]. At [m. 133] it reaches pp in D-flat major, the softest spot. A loud burst follows at [m. 137].

listening_points.headline: Dark keys, then G major
listening_points.text: The music slides through E-flat minor [m. 140], then C minor [m. 144]. Three instruments play together at [m. 146-147]. It then lands on G major [m. 148], which sets up the final section.

listening_points.headline: A new final section begins quietly
listening_points.text: A new section begins with a new key signature [m. 151]. It starts soft. The first violin probably leads. The music passes through D minor [m. 154] and gets loud at [m. 157].

listening_points.headline: Bright C major to the end
listening_points.text: The key turns to C major [m. 159]. The mood is now bright and happy. It stays loud. The lead seems to move between Violin 1, Violin 2 and the cello, and it is often unclear. The last bars are block chords [m. 186-188].

glossary.explanation: All instruments move together in the same rhythm, like block chords.
One instrument has the tune. The others support it.
The home note and scale of the music. Minor keys sound darker. Major keys sound brighter.
The sharps or flats written at the start of a line. It shows the key. A new one marks a change of key.
A sudden strong accent on one note or chord.
The main tune that you can recognize when it comes back.
